page: Microsoft Azure E16-4ds_v6 is an x86_64 architecture virtual machine belonging to the Edsv6 server family, virtualized via Microsoft Hyper-V. It features 4 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 2 physical Intel Xeon 8573C cores with hyper-threading. The processor operates at a base clock speed of 4.2 GHz and includes a 260 MB L3 cache. It is equipped with 128.0 GB of system memory, yielding a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 32.0 GB per vCPU. The instance includes 945 GB of local storage and supports Premium Storage. No GPUs are bundled with this configuration.

Benchmark results indicate strong single-core performance, with a Geekbench single-core score of 2093.0 and a strong text processing score of 2505.0. However, multi-core and memory bandwidth metrics show limitations. The stress-ng multi-core CPU performance is rated as weak at 3948.96, and the large-block memory read and write bandwidths are relatively low at 34.95 GB/sec and 24.77 GB/sec respectively. Redis SET operations achieved 5.57 million operations per second, which is positioned in the lower tier. LLM inference speeds are moderate for small models but drop to a poor 4.48 tokens per second for text generation on a medium 7B model.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the E16-4ds_v6 offers a dense memory allocation relative to its compute footprint, making it suitable for memory-bound workloads that do not require massive parallel processing. The primary tradeoff is the low core count and weaker multi-core scaling, which limits its utility for highly parallel compute-intensive tasks. The server is best suited for memory-intensive applications, small to medium databases, caching layers, and text processing tasks that benefit from large memory capacity and strong single-thread execution.
